subject: Japan: data localization pathways, evidence package and breach-notification playbook
messages:
From: Keiko Yamada <keiko.yamada@mitsui-tt.co.jp>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naoki Suzuki <naoki.suzuki@keplerbank.jp>
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 23:12:00 +0900
Subject: Japan residency & evidence request - KeplerBank RFP

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this on. KeplerBank has a few country-specific gating items in the RFP that they want evidence for before procurement can progress:

- Physical and logical location of processing for PII originating from Japan customers (in-country or pinned region).
- Encryption at-rest details and whether customer-managed keys (CMK) in Japan (ap-northeast-1) are supported.
- Audit logs: retention period, tenancy, and tamper-evidence controls.
- Breach notification SLA (initial alert and detailed report timeline).
- Network/data flow diagrams showing where inference happens vs. where logs/telemetry may egress.
- Any certifications/attestations (SOC 2, ISO 27001) and evidence for our legal team.

Can you attach whatever evidence you can share (playbook, diagrams, attestation PDFs) and outline the exact fallback behavior if Tokyo capacity is unavailable? The bank is particularly sensitive to cross-border egress, so please call out any circumstances where data would leave Japan and the controls in place.

Deadline: they asked for a package by COB Tokyo Tuesday (2027-05-11).

Thanks,
Keiko
KeplerBank - Procurement (on behalf of Mitsui Holdings)

--
Keiko Yamada
Senior Sourcing Manager
KeplerBank Japan
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Keiko Yamada <keiko.yamada@mitsui-tt.co.jp>
Cc: Naoki Suzuki <naoki.suzuki@keplerbank.jp>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 23:45:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Japan residency & evidence request - KeplerBank RFP

Keiko / Naoki — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a consolidated package and a short summary here. Attachments: RESIDENCY_PLAYBOOK_v2.pdf, Japan_RFP_Answers.docx.

Summary (high level):
- In-region primary: We offer a Tokyo region deployment (hosted: ap-northeast-1) where inference, model state (KV cache), and short-term logs remain in-region. For customers that require complete isolation, we offer Redwood Private (VPC) or an on-prem appliance; both support customer-managed KMS.
- Customer-managed keys (CMK): Supported. You can provision AWS KMS CMKs in ap-northeast-1 or integrate with a customer HSM/KMS. Keys can be set to never leave the region.
- Fallback behavior: By default, requests are routed to in-region capacity. Failover to Singapore (ap-southeast-1) only occurs under an explicit capacity-failover policy or by customer opt-in for cross-border burst. When failover happens, we log the event and notify the customer. We can also configure hard geofencing (no egress) if required for contract terms.
- Audit logs & retention: Tenant-isolated audit trails are available; standard retention is 90 days, extended retention options (365+ days) available as an add-on. Logs are digitally signed/timestamped for tamper-evidence.
- Encryption & transport: All storage and transport use strong encryption (AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit). Key usage audit logs are available and can be forwarded to customer SIEM.
- Breach notification: We commit to an initial notification within 24 hours of detection and a full incident report within 72 hours for incidents impacting customer data. We can negotiate shorter windows in SLAs for enterprise contracts.
- Certifications: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestations; redacted reports are included in the playbook.
- Provisioning timeline: For dedicated in-region capacity (Redwood Dedicated in Tokyo), typical provisioning is 2-4 weeks (depends on capacity and contract). Private/on-prem deployments vary (4-8 weeks).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether KeplerBank requires hard geofencing (no cross-border egress under any condition).
2) Let us know if the bank needs customer-managed KMS only (no Redwood key escrow).
3) We'll prepare a DocuSign addendum for any SLA tighter than our standard breach timelines.

I attached the playbook and a completed answers doc to address each RFP question. Happy to schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough Monday morning JST.

Best,
Olga
Head of Security & Compliance (EMEA/APAC)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RESIDENCY_PLAYBOOK_v2.pdf (redacted attestations, architecture diagrams), Japan_RFP_Answers.docx (question-by-question responses)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Keiko Yamada <keiko.yamada@mitsui-tt.co.jp>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Naoki Suzuki <naoki.suzuki@keplerbank.jp>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 08:10:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Japan residency & evidence request - KeplerBank RFP

Keiko — quick technical clarifications from engineering so we can finalize the diagram and the service-level addendum:

- "In-country processing": Our Tokyo serving nodes host model inference and ephemeral KV caches. We can configure the KV cache and model container scheduling to never evict to another region for the duration of a session. Long-term storage (checkpoints/backups) is configurable and can be set to remain in-region or move to customer-designated archival storage.
- KMS/HSM: We support AWS KMS CMKs in ap-northeast-1. For HSM integration, we provide a KMIP-compatible connector for customer HSM appliances; keys can be configured so that Redwood never imports or retains key material.
- Telemetry & telemetry anonymization: By default we collect minimal operational telemetry for reliability. We can enable a pseudonymization pipeline that strips direct PII before any cross-region telemetry egress. Please confirm whether tokenized/anonymized telemetry is acceptable for KeplerBank's security team.
- Network topology: Attached is edge-routing-diagram.png showing how traffic enters a Tokyo edge, where model inference runs, and the conditions under which control-plane calls may cross-region (e.g., global model catalog queries).

Questions for KeplerBank:
1) Is any element of the request strictly required to be processed on-prem (e.g., tokenization step) or is a VPC-hosted Redwood Private deployment acceptable?
2) Can we assume acceptability of pseudonymized telemetry for reliability debugging?

I'll update the Japan_RFP_Answers doc to include these clarifications once you confirm.

—Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: edge-routing-diagram.png
From: Keiko Yamada <keiko.yamada@mitsui-tt.co.jp>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naoki Suzuki <naoki.suzuki@keplerbank.jp>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 10:05:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Japan residency & evidence request - KeplerBank RFP

Olga / Jonas — this is very helpful, thank you. A few quick answers and next asks:

- KeplerBank is leaning toward a VPC-hosted Redwood Private deployment but may require an initial on-prem tokenization step for a pilot. Please include on-prem tokenization as an optional line item in the addendum.
- Pseudonymized telemetry: acceptable for debugging provided that no direct identifiers leave Japan and we get a short spec of the pseudonymization process (hashing/salting, retention).
- Breach notification SLA: procurement asked whether Redwood can commit to 24-hour initial notification in the contract (not just as an operational target). Can you confirm and, if so, prepare a DocuSign SLA addendum?
- Logistics: Procurement needs the final package and the DocuSign by COB Tokyo Tuesday (2027-05-11). Attached is a short addendum from KeplerBank (Kepler_RFP_Addendum.pdf) that lists procurement contact and invoice remit info.

If you can send the SLA addendum draft this afternoon JST, we'll route internally for signature.

Best,
Keiko

Attachment: Kepler_RFP_Addendum.pdf
